records.description: For light-particle processes below the heavy production thresholds, a consistently matched EFT can omit the heavy field as an explicit low-energy degree of freedom while retaining its virtual effects in local coefficients and renormalized light parameters. In a controlled expansion with light scales E much smaller than M and non-growing dimensionless matching coefficients, higher-dimensional contributions are suppressed by powers of E/M. This conditional suppression does not erase heavy-field effects in the relevant or marginal sector.
records.name: Conditional heavy-field decoupling
openObligations: MSbar beta functions of the full theory do not automatically discard a massive field when mu passes its mass. One changes the field content and matches at the threshold before applying the lower-energy RG evolution.

Taking a heavy mass large while its coupling also grows, including masses tied to symmetry breaking, need not satisfy the stated suppression assumptions. The review's top-loop discussion is a formal warning, not an admitted numerical Zbb calculation or independent experimental test of nondecoupling.

Near a production threshold or resonance, or without the stated scale separation and power counting, the local truncation need not apply. Integrating out a heavy degree of freedom does not make the full theory physically disappear or create a sharp universal spatial cutoff.

No new observed composite, stable carrier, time-directed formation process or universal minimal number of constituents follows from changing an effective description. Internal heavy propagation is an amplitude contribution, not a counted population of virtual particles.

records.description: The reported calculation uses a 24^3 x 48 lattice, a=0.145 fm, three degenerate clover flavors and a tree-level-improved Luscher-Weisz gauge action at pion mass approximately 800 MeV. It analyzes 16,368 configurations from 17 streams, bins 50 saved configurations for residual autocorrelation, and computes approximately 2.12 x 10^7 sparse-source propagators. A subset of gauge fields was also used in Beane2013. Zero-total-momentum dibaryon and local hexaquark operators probe I=1 A1+ and I=0 T1+ sectors. The source compares GEVP, symmetric/block Lanczos and asymmetric-correlator analyses of these related correlators.
records.name: Detmold heavy-mass state-identification analysis
openObligations: The 2026 calculation is not a new independent repeat of all three 2013 volumes. Shared gauge fields, action and scale coexist with changed propagator sampling, operators and analysis. Configurations and propagators are not independent experimental events.

Treating finite-time energy estimators as eigenvalues requires the stated N-state-saturation assumption. Symmetric variational upper bounds do not exclude missed lower levels. Residual bounds require a Hermitian transfer matrix and delimit a window containing some eigenvalue, not necessarily the ground state; for this improved action the source restricts Hermiticity to its low-energy sector, E much less than 1/a.

Tighter gap bounds require the stated no-missing-states threshold and negligible thermal effects. Estimates based on noninteracting NN level counts below NDelta or DeltaDelta thresholds can fail if extra low states are present. Source errors and bound widths are distinct; one-sided upper bounds cannot supply two-sided phase errors.

The selected phase comparison truncates to the lowest S wave, neglects lattice artifacts and does not determine a complete coupled-channel amplitude. Raw correlators, residual/gap calculations, operator completeness, continuum/infinite-volume extrapolations and physical-mass nuclear binding are not reproduced here.

limitations: The channel is an isolated ground-state bare deuteron with no supplied energy and asymptotically free p+p+e-+electron-antineutrino final particles. Its net charge is +1 on both sides. Neutral atoms, electronic bound final states, molecular ions and externally driven breakup are different state specifications.

Q0 neglects the antineutrino rest mass; any nonnegative final neutrino mass raises the required rest energy. Positive-energy on-shell final particles and four-momentum conservation make Q0<0 an exclusion for this channel. Q0>=0 alone would not establish a nonzero matrix element or rate.

The calculation uses the one Rau joint adjusted pair mp=1.007276466580(17)u and md=2.013553212537(16)u with correlation +0.26. These reuse the published mass measurements and molecular/reference inputs; the local adjustment, direct deuteron and earlier proton values are not substituted or pooled as independent replicas.

The adopted CODATA 2018 inputs are me=0.000548579909065(16)u and u*c^2=931494102.42(28)eV. They are external adjustment values, not new electron-mass or energy-conversion measurements; this calculation does not update them to a later adjustment.

The admitted neutron mass was inferred as mn=md-mp+Bd/c^2 using the same adjusted masses and capture binding. Substitution into (mn-mp-me)c^2-Bd cancels Bd identically. Capture-derived mn and Bd are not independent confirmation of the reduced Q and cannot be assigned independent errors in that expression.

Separately inserting printed mn=1.00866491604u and Bd/c^2=0.00238817008u gives a Q larger by 0.0027944823...eV than the reduced expression. The identity gives mn=1.008664916037u, compatible with the printed neutron rounding; the difference is not a source-analysis error or a second acquisition. The display-rounding box is not a confidence interval.

The published +0.26 mass-pair correlation enters var(md-2mp)=var(md)+4var(mp)-4cov(md,mp), giving about 0.0313eV standard uncertainty for this contribution alone. Electron/reference cross-covariances and the full adjustment are not reconstructed; no complete Q uncertainty, discovery significance or calibrated coverage is supplied.

Bare nuclear masses cannot be replaced by neutral hydrogen-isotope masses. For positive electronic binding energies IH and ID, Q0=[M(D)-2M(H)]c^2+ID-2IH. This identity retains the declared bare-particle channel; it does not import a neutral-atom decay or its final electronic states.

This is a new bounded calculation from published inputs, not a beta-decay measurement reported by Rau. It establishes neither all-channel deuteron permanence, a nuclear or individual bound-neutron lifetime, nor stability of arbitrary nuclei. No weak amplitude, phase-space rate, raw mass fit, instrument calibration or complete covariance is reproduced.

records.description: Adopt the selected equilibrium continuum-solvent ion-atmosphere model in its original electrostatic-cgs units. Let n_i be bulk ion-species number density, z_i signed valence, D the dimensionless solvent dielectric constant, kT thermal energy and e the positive charge magnitude. For electroneutral bulk sum_i(n_i*z_i)=0, the Boltzmann density n_i(r)=n_i*exp[-z_i*e*psi(r)/(kT)] gives, after weak-potential linearization, nabla^2*psi=kappa^2*psi outside the tagged source, with kappa^2=4*pi*e^2*sum_i(n_i*z_i^2)/(D*kT). In the dilute point-ion limiting model the tagged-charge mean potential is psi(r)=q*exp(-kappa*r)/(D*r). The screening length 1/kappa depends on composition, temperature and solvent response; it represents statistical ion-atmosphere structure rather than an ion-formation event.

The input ion species, valences, concentrations, continuum solvent and thermal equilibrium are supplied. Linearization needs |z_i*e*psi| small relative to kT; the point-ion law is a dilute limiting model, not a controlled microscopic near-core or concentrated-electrolyte potential.

studies.finding: The paired 2026 preprints leave the nature of the lowest I=1 and I=0 two-nucleon states at these heavy-mass action parameters unresolved without additional spectral assumptions. GEVP and Lanczos agree for the same correlator data, while different operator choices under N-state saturation yield inconsistent energy estimates; the wider two-sided bounds remain compatible. The authors find no positive I=1 bound-state evidence from those bounds, and the I=0 level is too near the bound-state threshold to settle its nature from this one volume. This does not exclude a missed bound state or validate the earlier binding assignment as consensus.
limitations: The 2026 calculation is not a new independent repeat of all three 2013 volumes. Shared gauge fields, action and scale coexist with changed propagator sampling, operators and analysis. Configurations and propagators are not independent experimental events.

Treating finite-time energy estimators as eigenvalues requires the stated N-state-saturation assumption. Symmetric variational upper bounds do not exclude missed lower levels. Residual bounds require a Hermitian transfer matrix and delimit a window containing some eigenvalue, not necessarily the ground state; for this improved action the source restricts Hermiticity to its low-energy sector, E much less than 1/a.

Tighter gap bounds require the stated no-missing-states threshold and negligible thermal effects. Estimates based on noninteracting NN level counts below NDelta or DeltaDelta thresholds can fail if extra low states are present. Source errors and bound widths are distinct; one-sided upper bounds cannot supply two-sided phase errors.

The selected phase comparison truncates to the lowest S wave, neglects lattice artifacts and does not determine a complete coupled-channel amplitude. Raw correlators, residual/gap calculations, operator completeness, continuum/infinite-volume extrapolations and physical-mass nuclear binding are not reproduced here.

This record synthesizes the reported primary numerical analysis and its methodological conclusion. It is neither a new measured energy nor an independent simulation; the two preprints describe the same work and are not pooled confirmations.

A negative finite-volume energy shift relative to two nucleons is not by itself an infinite-volume bound-state determination. Residual/gap intervals can contain an eigenvalue without establishing its ground-state index or excluding additional levels outside the interval. The source tables distinguish statistical confidence from assumption-dependent spectral windows.

The asymmetric-correlator diagnostics show changing left/right state overlaps over accessible Euclidean times. They question the eigenstate interpretation of apparently stable estimators without proving that every such energy estimate is wrong or that a bound state cannot exist.

The reported synthetic small-gap examples use chosen spectra, overlaps and a noise model related to the lattice data. Their statistically similar bound/scattering outputs illustrate an inverse-problem ambiguity; they are not additional QCD measurements or a unique reconstruction of the true spectrum.

Neither the single-volume 2026 analysis nor the conditional 2013 interpretation establishes continuum physical-mass nuclear binding, all nuclei, atomic binding, a real-time formation rate or permanent matter stability.
